name: Federal family portal: Zeit, die prägt (national campaign for foster families)
coverage: Germany (national information campaign by the federal family ministry)
notes: Information only. The portal sends people to their youth welfare office (Jugendamt) and its foster care service. It says these services hold regular information events. A postcode search finds the local office.

name: PFAD Bundesverband der Pflege- und Adoptivfamilien e.V.
coverage: Germany (national federation of foster and adoptive family groups, with Land associations and local groups)
notes: Represents foster and adoptive families; it does not approve carers. Founded in 1976. Its Land associations and local groups support families.

name: KVJS Land Youth Office Baden-Württemberg: foster care and central adoption office (Pflegekinderhilfe; Zentrale Adoptionsstelle)
coverage: Baden-Württemberg (Land youth office of the Kommunalverband für Jugend und Soziales)
notes: Advises youth welfare offices and publishes a guide for foster parents that sends readers to their local office. Per search results, its central adoption office handles international adoption for people living in the Land.

name: City of Heidelberg: adoption and foster care service (Adoptions- und Pflegestellen)
notes: First comes an information talk with the foster care service and an information pack. Further personal talks follow for those who apply. The page says foster parents should be over 25.

name: City of Karlsruhe social and youth office: foster care and adoption service (Pflegekinderdienst und Adoptionsvermittlungsstelle)
notes: People call for a free information talk. The page also lists an information evening with the adult education centre (VHS). People who live in Karlsruhe apply to the city's adoption unit.

name: Ludwigsburg district youth welfare office: adoption
notes: People email to arrange an information talk; the page also mentions an information evening. It asks applicants to be married and to have lived together for some time.

name: Ludwigsburg district youth welfare office: foster care service (Pflegekinderdienst)
notes: The service starts with a free information talk, then preparation with a compact seminar, then placement.

name: City of Mannheim youth welfare office: foster care and adoption service (Pflegekinderdienst/Adoptionsvermittlung)
notes: The page invites questions in a personal talk and gives phone and email. Flyers in several languages.

name: City of Stuttgart youth welfare office: foster care service (Pflegekinderdienst)
notes: Information events run each spring and autumn. The page links to the regional guide for foster parents from the Land youth office (KVJS).

name: Bavarian Land Youth Office (ZBFS): central adoption office (Zentrale Adoptionsstelle)
notes: For adoption within Germany, people go to the adoption office of the youth welfare office where they live (AdVermiG section 9b). The central office supports local offices and handles international adoption.

name: City of Augsburg office for children, youth and family: foster children and adoption unit (Fachbereich Pflegekinder und Adoptionen)
notes: Seen in search results; the city service page returned 404. A city flyer dated August 2025 offers a personal getting-to-know-you talk.

name: City of Munich youth welfare office (Stadtjugendamt): becoming foster parents
notes: A free information evening runs every month. People sign up by email or by a printed reply card. The Sozialreferat has a general contact form, not one for fostering.

name: City of Nuremberg youth welfare office: full-time foster care unit (Fachstelle Vollzeitpflege)
notes: The contact form is the one linked from the foster care unit's contact box. The page links to information evenings and to 2 non-profit partners (Rummelsberger Diakonie and SOS-Kinderdorf).

name: City of Regensburg adoption office (Adoptionsvermittlungsstelle)
notes: Listed in the Bavarian Land youth office directory. The city also publishes a leaflet looking for foster parents (seen in search results).

name: Joint adoption office of the city of Würzburg and Kitzingen and Würzburg districts
coverage: City of Würzburg, Kitzingen district and Würzburg district
notes: Listed in the Bavarian Land youth office directory of adoption offices. People apply to the office for the place where they live.

name: Catholic Youth Care, Bavaria (KJF): adoption service Augsburg (Adoptionsdienst)
notes: Listed by the Bavarian Land youth office as an approved non-profit adoption office for adoption within Germany. Own website not checked.

name: Rummelsberger Diakonie: foster care service (Pflegekinderdienst)
coverage: Nuremberg area (partner of the city youth welfare office)
notes: The page carries its own contact form. Linked from the Nuremberg youth welfare office foster care page.

name: Social Service of Catholic Women (SkF) Nuremberg-Fürth: adoption placement
coverage: Nuremberg and Fürth area (approved non-profit adoption office)
notes: Listed by the Bavarian Land youth office as an approved non-profit adoption office. A search summary says the SkF also recruits foster families for Nuremberg.

name: SOS-Kinderdorf Nürnberg: foster care service (Pflegekinderdienst)
coverage: Nuremberg area (partner of the city youth welfare office)
notes: Linked from the Nuremberg youth welfare office foster care page. No form found on the page.

name: Senate Department for Education, Youth and Family: adoption placement office (Adoptionsvermittlungsstelle)
coverage: Berlin: one adoption office for all 12 district youth welfare offices
notes: The page says this office does adoption placement for all 12 Berlin districts. It offers advice and information talks, and runs the suitability check. Contact is by phone, email or appointment.

name: Senate Department for Education, Youth and Family: foster children (Pflegekinder)
coverage: Berlin (Land overview; placements run by the 12 district youth welfare offices)
notes: Overview page. It links to the Familien für Kinder portal for information evenings and the one-off start bonus. Each district's foster care service assesses applicants.

name: Mitte district youth welfare office (Jugendamt Mitte): foster care service
notes: The page sends people to the information evenings of Familien für Kinder. A follow-up preparation seminar there is compulsory.

name: Neukölln district youth welfare office: foster care network (PflegeKinderHilfe Neukölln)
notes: A network of the youth welfare office and 2 non-profit providers.

name: Pankow district youth welfare office (Jugendamt Pankow): foster care service
notes: The page runs a campaign for Pankow foster parents and gives contact details.

name: Reinickendorf district youth welfare office: foster children (Pflegekinder in Reinickendorf)
notes: The page asks people who want to foster to contact the district's partner organisation. It also offers a podcast with foster parents.

name: Familien für Kinder gGmbH: Pflegekinder Berlin (information evenings and preparation seminar)
coverage: Berlin (city-wide information portal and preparation for foster families)
notes: Information evenings run about every 2 weeks; the next listed is 1 December 2026. Sign-up is on the page. A one-day preparation seminar follows. The site says about 9 months pass from the first evening to a placement. The Berlin Senate page links to this portal.

name: Central Adoption Office Berlin-Brandenburg (Zentrale Adoptionsstelle Berlin-Brandenburg, ZABB)
coverage: Berlin and Brandenburg (joint central adoption office at the Brandenburg education, youth and sport ministry)
notes: Supports public and non-profit adoption offices in both Länder and handles international adoption. The ministry pages explain the adoption process and list seminars. Per search results, international cases carry a 1,200 euro fee.

name: Oberhavel district: foster families (Pflegefamilien)
notes: Steps: people get in touch, then a personal information talk. Passing the applicant seminar is required. The contact form linked is the district's general one.

name: Joint foster care service of Potsdam and Potsdam-Mittelmark district (Gemeinsame Fachstelle Pflegekinderdienst)
coverage: City of Potsdam and Potsdam-Mittelmark district
notes: We read the city's page on what foster parents need. The service page itself reset the connection. Applicants take an applicant seminar before a placement (per a search summary).

name: Spree-Neiße district youth welfare office: foster care service (Pflegekinderdienst)
notes: A separate website for the foster care service, with sections on types of care and the application process.

name: Bremen Office for Social Services (Amt für Soziale Dienste): becoming foster parents (Pflegeeltern werden)
notes: Bremen service portal entry, seen in search results; the portal refused our reader (403). Per the summary, people can apply online with a form called Pflegeeltern werden.

name: PiB – Pflegekinder in Bremen gGmbH
coverage: City of Bremen (assesses and supports foster families for the Bremen youth welfare office)
notes: A free information evening on full-time foster care runs on the first Tuesday of each month, some online. The Bremen service portal says PiB checks whether applicants are suitable.

name: Hamburg Authority for Schools, Family and Vocational Education: foster children (Pflegekinder)
coverage: Hamburg (Land overview; 7 district foster care services)
notes: The page says the education centre for Hamburg foster families (Bildungszentrum Hamburger Pflegefamilien und Patenschaften) runs regular information events. District foster care services give advice.

name: Joint Central Adoption Office (Gemeinsame Zentrale Adoptionsstelle, GZA)
coverage: Bremen, Hamburg, Lower Saxony and Schleswig-Holstein (joint central adoption office of 4 Länder)
notes: One of 12 central adoption offices in Germany. It handles international adoption and advises services. Advice by phone, email or appointment. The page lists information evenings on adoption and fostering; the latest date shown is 9 October 2024.

name: District office Altona: foster care service (bezirklicher Pflegekinderdienst)
coverage: Hamburg-Altona district; also applicants in Pinneberg and Stade districts who want to foster a Hamburg child
notes: Each Hamburg district has its own foster care service. The page invites people to get in touch and lists named staff contacts. It also serves people outside Hamburg who want to foster a Hamburg child.

name: District office Eimsbüttel: foster care service (bezirklicher Pflegekinderdienst)
coverage: Hamburg-Eimsbüttel district; also families in Dithmarschen, Flensburg, Neumünster, Nordfriesland, Rendsburg-Eckernförde, Schleswig and Segeberg
notes: Each Hamburg district has its own foster care service. The page invites people to get in touch and lists named staff contacts. It also serves people outside Hamburg who want to foster a Hamburg child.

name: District office Harburg: foster care service (bezirklicher Pflegekinderdienst)
coverage: Hamburg-Harburg district; also nearby districts including Bremen, Bremerhaven, Celle, Cuxhaven, Rotenburg (Wümme) and Verden
notes: Each Hamburg district has its own foster care service. The page invites people to get in touch and lists named staff contacts. It also serves people outside Hamburg who want to foster a Hamburg child.

name: District office Hamburg-Nord: foster care service (bezirklicher Pflegekinderdienst)
coverage: Hamburg-Nord district; also families in Kiel, Norderstedt, Plön and Steinburg
notes: Each Hamburg district has its own foster care service. The page invites people to get in touch and lists named staff contacts. It also serves people outside Hamburg who want to foster a Hamburg child.

name: District office Wandsbek: foster care service (bezirklicher Pflegekinderdienst)
coverage: Hamburg-Wandsbek district; also families in Herzogtum Lauenburg, Lübeck, Ostholstein, Stormarn and western Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania
notes: Each Hamburg district has its own foster care service. The page invites people to get in touch and lists named staff contacts. It also serves people outside Hamburg who want to foster a Hamburg child.

name: PFIFF gGmbH: education centre for Hamburg foster families (Bildungszentrum Hamburger Pflegefamilien und Patenschaften)
coverage: Hamburg (information events and training for foster families on behalf of the city)
notes: Runs information events for people thinking about fostering, and free training for carers. The home page has a general contact form that asks for place of residence.

name: Joint adoption office of Darmstadt-Dieburg district, the city of Darmstadt and Odenwaldkreis
coverage: Darmstadt-Dieburg district, City of Darmstadt and Odenwaldkreis
notes: Listed in the directory of adoption offices in Hesse (dated March 2026) from the joint central adoption office. Own website not checked.

name: City of Frankfurt youth and social welfare office: foster care service (Pflegekinderdienst/Vollzeitpflege)
notes: Per the search summary, an online information evening runs on the second Tuesday of each month; sign-up by email or phone. The page refused our reader (403).

name: Joint adoption office of Fulda district, the city of Fulda and Hersfeld-Rotenburg district
coverage: Fulda district, City of Fulda and Hersfeld-Rotenburg district
notes: Listed in the directory of adoption offices in Hesse (dated March 2026) from the joint central adoption office. Own website not checked.

name: Joint adoption office of the Kassel region (city and district of Kassel)
coverage: City of Kassel and Kassel district
notes: Listed in the directory of adoption offices in Hesse (dated March 2026) from the joint central adoption office. Own website not checked.

name: City of Offenbach youth welfare office: adoption placement
notes: Listed in the directory of adoption offices in Hesse (dated March 2026) from the joint central adoption office. Own website not checked.

name: City of Wiesbaden social work office (Amt für Soziale Arbeit): foster care service
notes: The application to take a foster child is a PDF, not an online form. City press releases announce information evenings (seen in search results).

name: Social Service of Catholic Women (SkF) Fulda: adoption placement
notes: Listed in the directory of adoption offices in Hesse (dated March 2026) from the joint central adoption office. Own website not checked.

name: City of Hannover youth welfare office: foster care service (Pflegekinderdienst)
notes: People interested in fostering are invited to an information event. One evening focuses on children with special needs. The city and the Hannover Region run separate services.

name: Helmstedt district youth welfare office: foster care service (Pflegekinderdienst)
notes: The district brochure says the first step is a talk with your own youth welfare office's foster care service, or an approved agency. Its payment figures are dated 2017.

name: Osnabrück district: adoption and foster care service (Adoptions- und Pflegekinderwesen)
notes: The district adoption office advises on all adoption questions and supports families before and after adoption.

name: Hannover Region youth welfare office: adoption office (Adoptionsvermittlungsstelle der Region Hannover)
notes: Information events run about 4 times a year; dates by phone or email. People can apply only after attending. The application forms are handed out at the event.

name: Hannover Region youth welfare office: foster care service (Pflegekinderdienst der Region Hannover)
coverage: Hannover Region (towns without their own youth welfare office)
notes: Free information evenings run in several towns. A special event on 28 January 2027 is for families for children with extra needs. The Region also has its own adoption office.

name: Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania Land Youth Office (LAGuS): central adoption office (Zentrale Adoptionsstelle)
notes: The first place to ask about international adoption. It also advises local adoption offices. Since January 2026 the Land youth office is part of the Land office for health and social affairs (LAGuS), per search results.

name: City of Rostock youth welfare office: becoming foster parents (Pflegeeltern werden)
notes: Life-event page with links to services. A search summary says Rostock foster carers must attend at least 2 training events a year.

name: City of Schwerin youth welfare office: foster care service (Pflegekinderdienst)
notes: People contact the youth welfare office or foster care service first. Information events are free and carry no obligation. A course and a written application follow. A city news item (search result) names a 40-hour preparation course run by the non-profit Pro Kind.

name: Vorpommern-Greifswald district youth welfare office: foster care service (Pflegekinderdienst)
notes: The page invites contact, including through a contact form for the foster care service. It works with Caritas in Vorpommern on events and training.

name: Pro Kind e.V. Schwerin: preparation course and support for foster families
coverage: City of Schwerin (works with the city youth welfare office)
notes: A city news item says Pro Kind takes questions and sign-ups for the preparation course in person or by phone. The item is old.

name: LVR Youth Office Rhineland: central adoption office (Zentrale Adoptionsstelle)
coverage: Rhineland (regional youth office of the Landschaftsverband Rheinland)
notes: Mainly international adoption. Per search results, it runs information evenings on international adoption and a preparation seminar for applicants (20 and 21 November 2026).

name: LWL Youth Office Westphalia: central adoption office (Zentrale Adoptionsstelle)
coverage: Westphalia-Lippe (regional youth office of the Landschaftsverband Westfalen-Lippe)
notes: Advises people who want to adopt, mainly on international adoption, and helps adopted people trace their origins. It runs information events and seminars on international adoption.

name: City of Dortmund youth welfare office: foster care and adoption service (Pflegekinderhilfe und Adoptionsdienst)
notes: The page offers an online contact form for fostering, short-term fostering and adoption. It also lists information events from 10 December 2026 to 25 November 2027.

name: City of Düsseldorf youth welfare office: foster care service (Pflegekinderdienst)
notes: Information events are listed. People sign up by email or phone, or just come. A preparation seminar of 5 dates runs twice a year.

name: City of Duisburg youth welfare office: foster care and adoption service
notes: The page we read covers short-term emergency foster care. Applicants are trained in one-to-one and group sessions. It links a sheet on applicant training.

name: City of Essen youth welfare office: foster care service (Pflegekinderdienst)
notes: The city offers open advice days for people who want to find out more. Several talks with a worker are followed by 2 weekend seminars.

name: City of Cologne youth welfare office: foster care service (Pflegekinderdienst)
notes: The page asks people to get in touch first. It offers an online application to take a foster child and a secure contact form. Preparation is 4 seminar days over about 6 months. On 20 November 2026 the page still showed the 2025 payment rates.

name: Soest district: joint adoption office (Gemeinsame Adoptionsvermittlungsstelle, GAVS)
notes: Advises people who want to adopt and parents thinking about adoption. The page carries an adoption contact form.

name: SKFM Düsseldorf (Catholic social service for women, men and families): adoption and foster care service
notes: We read the home page only. Search results say it runs an adoption and foster care service alongside the city service and Diakonie.

name: Joint Central Adoption Office of Rhineland-Palatinate and Hesse (Gemeinsame Zentrale Adoptionsstelle, LSJV)
coverage: Rhineland-Palatinate and Hesse (joint central adoption office at the Land office for social affairs, youth and care in Mainz)
notes: Seen in search results. Local adoption offices and approved non-profit offices handle adoption within Germany. The joint office handles international adoption and gives general advice. It also works with Saarland.

name: City of Kaiserslautern youth welfare office: joint adoption office
coverage: City of Kaiserslautern and partner districts
notes: Listed in the directory of adoption offices in Rhineland-Palatinate (dated November 2025) from the Land youth office. Own website not checked.

name: Kusel district youth welfare office: foster care service (Pflegekinderdienst)
notes: The page invites people to get in touch for a free first talk.

name: City of Mainz youth and family office: foster care service (Pflegekinderdienst)
notes: Advice is in a personal talk. The youth welfare office checks suitability, then a compulsory preparation course follows.

name: Mayen-Koblenz district youth welfare office: joint adoption office with the city of Koblenz
coverage: Mayen-Koblenz district and City of Koblenz
notes: Listed in the directory of adoption offices in Rhineland-Palatinate (dated November 2025) from the Land youth office. Own website not checked.

name: City of Trier youth welfare office: joint adoption office with neighbouring districts
coverage: City of Trier and neighbouring districts
notes: Listed in the directory of adoption offices in Rhineland-Palatinate (dated November 2025) from the Land youth office. Own website not checked.

name: Social Service of Catholic Women (SkF) Koblenz: adoption placement
notes: Listed in the directory of adoption offices in Rhineland-Palatinate (dated November 2025) from the Land youth office. Own website not checked.

name: Saarland Land Youth Office (Landesjugendamt): central adoption office
notes: Seen in search results; the Land site refused our reader (403). Per the summary, the central adoption office looks for suitable parents for children who may be adopted.

name: Neunkirchen district youth welfare office: foster care service (Pflegekinderdienst, PKD)
notes: The service takes applications from people who want to foster, checks suitability, places children and supports families.

name: Saarbrücken Regional Association youth welfare office: adoption
notes: The process includes documents, a home visit and a compulsory weekend seminar run by the youth welfare office.

name: Saarbrücken Regional Association youth welfare office: full-time foster care (Pflegeeltern – Vollzeitpflege)
notes: The page describes full-time foster care and the foster care service.

name: Saarlouis district youth welfare office: foster care service (Pflegekinderdienst)
notes: The service holds information events at the district office. On 20 November 2026 the page said new dates would follow next year; the last report is of 23 January 2025.

name: Saarpfalz district: foster care service and adoption office (Pflegekinderdienst und Adoptionsvermittlungsstelle)
notes: Combined page for fostering and adoption. Little detail on the first step.

name: Saxony Land Youth Office: central adoption office (Zentrale Adoptionsstelle)
notes: Supports local adoption offices, mainly for children with special needs, international adoption and hard cases. People who want to adopt go to the adoption office of their own youth welfare office.

name: City of Chemnitz youth welfare office: foster care service
notes: We read the English page; it lists the service but little detail. Per search results, Caritas Chemnitz runs regular information evenings, the next on 28 January 2027.

name: City of Dresden youth welfare office: foster parent advice (Pflegeelternberatung)
notes: Information evenings run every 2 months with the office's partner organisations. Diakonie Dresden runs a programme of events for foster families.

name: City of Leipzig youth and family office: foster care and adoption service (Pflegekinderdienst/Adoption)
notes: Step 1 is a monthly first information evening; step 2 is a first talk with the service. The page links to a sign-up for the evening. Training is 3 Thursday evenings in a row.

name: Diakonie – Stadtmission Dresden: foster children in Dresden (Pflegekinder in Dresden)
coverage: City of Dresden (partner of the city youth welfare office)
notes: Its 2026 programme lists information evenings on Wednesdays, some online, and a preparation course for future foster parents.

name: Saxony-Anhalt Land Administration Office, Land Youth Office: central adoption office (Zentrale Adoptionsstelle)
notes: Advises local adoption offices on hard cases, international adoption and children with special needs. Search results show 2 different addresses for the office.

name: Börde district youth welfare office: foster care (Pflegekinderwesen Landkreis Börde)
notes: A separate website on fostering, with pages on types of care and on becoming foster parents.

name: City of Halle (Saale): foster care and adoption service (Pflegekinderdienst/Adoptionsvermittlung)
notes: An information event for applicants runs on the first Tuesday of each month. Contact forms on the page are tied to each staff contact.

name: City of Magdeburg youth welfare office: foster care service (Pflegekinderdienst)
notes: People first contact the service by phone or email. A first talk goes through forms and papers. Further talks, a home visit and an applicant seminar follow. A general city contact form is linked.

name: City of Flensburg: adoption and foster children (Adoptionen und Pflegekinder) – taking in foster children
notes: Online information evenings need no sign-up. A preparation course for approved foster parents runs from 19 March to 8 May 2027.

name: City of Kiel youth welfare office: foster care service (Pflegekinderdienst)
notes: The page invites couples and single people to an information evening.

name: Hanseatic City of Lübeck youth welfare office: foster child and adoption service (Pflegekinder- und Adoptionsstelle)
notes: Seen in search results; the page reset the connection. Per the summary, the full application takes about 6 months, with courses, a home visit and closing talks.

name: Rendsburg-Eckernförde district youth welfare office: foster parents and foster children
notes: The district magazine (2024) describes an information evening, then a written application with a life story, photos, police certificate and doctor's note. A preparation seminar runs twice a year.

name: Thuringia Land Youth Office (Landesjugendamt): central adoption office
coverage: Thuringia (Land youth office within the social affairs ministry)
notes: The Land youth office is the central adoption office. Per the Thuringia service portal, local youth welfare offices run the general suitability check.

name: Altenburger Land district youth welfare office: adoption and foster care service
notes: The district sheet on the foster care permit says an information talk follows first contact. It was written for people taking in children from Ukraine.

name: City of Erfurt youth welfare office: adoption and foster child placement (Adoptions- und Pflegekindervermittlungsstelle)
notes: Seen in search results only; the page reset the connection. City news items describe talks, groups, seminars and supervision for foster families.
